faqA1: No. Scan the QR with a phone camera. The menu opens in a browser.
faqQ2: Does a price change require a new QR?
faqA2: No. Product edits appear in your published menu. Design drafts become visible only after you publish them.
faqA3: The restaurant must enable ordering and publish its menu, and the guest must open an active table QR.
faqA4: Guest orders are currently paid at the restaurant. Platform subscriptions are confirmed by an administrator.
faqQ5: Do all templates support the same features?
faqA5: Yes. Search, languages, product details, and the cart are shared. The presentation and layout differ.
faqA6: Only within their assigned permissions. Cashiers see orders for their assigned branches.
contactNote: Tell us what you need. Your message will be saved in our support inbox.
privacyText1: Accounts store a name, email, protected authentication records, and sessions. Restaurant data is available to authorized staff. Published menus are public.
privacyText2: Carts are stored in this browser. Receipt access is kept in the current browser session. Orders do not require a guest account, name, or phone number. Avoid unnecessary personal details in order notes.
privacyText3: QR, menu, product, and cart events record language and time. They contain no IP address, name, or persistent guest identifier. Browsers can block analytics, so visit counts are approximate.
privacyText4: The contact form stores your name, email, and message. Limited session and rate-control records help protect the service. Use the contact page for data-related requests.
analyticsPrivacy: Visit counts are approximate; no guest identity is stored. Dates use UTC.
orderMetricsHint: Amounts represent order value and do not confirm payment collection.
